attacks.claim: Nightly job was tested at 12,000 users in 41 minutes. The plan's own sizing assumption (30% of 2.1M MAU, ~630k users) is ~52x that, implying ~36 hours at linear scaling, far beyond a nightly window. It runs as one SQL statement on the primary that also serves writes, risking lock/IO contention, replication lag and outage for the whole app.
attacks.evidence: "12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes" / "30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days" / "single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary"

attacks.claim: Full recompute of all 340k recipes for every pantry user nightly, with no incremental recompute (only changed pantries), candidate pruning, batching, or use of read replicas. Cost grows with users x catalog.
attacks.evidence: "for each user with a pantry, score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes)"

attacks.claim: The feature is gated behind entering 15 items with expiry dates, which is exactly the setup/typing friction behind the top churn reason (38%). Most users will never reach unlock, so the feature will deliver no value to them. The 25%-unlock goal is implausible without evidence.
attacks.evidence: "unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates" / "Too much setup / typing to get useful suggestions — 38%"

attacks.claim: Success target (25% of MAU unlocked in 60 days) is nearly equal to the sizing assumption (30% creating a pantry in 90 days). It implicitly assumes almost all pantry creators complete 15 dated items, which has no supporting data or prototype. Timing result also uses synthetic users only.
attacks.evidence: "25% of MAU unlock Pantry Match within 60 days" / "Adoption assumption for sizing: 30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days"

attacks.claim: No failure handling for the nightly job: no idempotency, chunking, timeout, retry, overrun protection or alerting. A killed or overrunning statement leaves stale or partial matches, or holds long transactions on the primary.
attacks.evidence: "PantryMatchJob (Sidekiq, nightly 02:00 UTC)" / "then upsert the top 50 into pantry_matches"

attacks.claim: Scoring is underspecified: expiry weighting function, handling of items with no expiry, and quantity/unit use are all undefined. Quantities and units are collected and users are prompted to update them, but never used in the score. Staples always present lets trivial recipes score 100%.
attacks.evidence: "weighted by expiry proximity, with pantry staples (salt, oil, water, pepper) always counted as present"

attacks.claim: New personal data (pantry contents, cooking behavior) has no retention, deletion, or export handling stated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention or deletion policy for pantry_items

attacks.claim: No feature flag or kill switch is described beyond 5%→100% rollout; no removal path for the new tables and job.
No compute budget or cost estimate for the nightly job at projected scale.
Beta and full rollout both in week 6 leave no time to observe job behavior at real scale before 100%. The scoring job is built before any real pantry data exists.
